item.title: France's mounting debt crisis raises risk of fresh Eurozone turmoil, warns Jefferies
item.description: France's mounting government debt and rising bond yields could trigger a fresh crisis at the heart of the Eurozone, with the risk of financial contagion threatening the stability of the common ...
item.content:encoded:
France's mounting debt crisis raises risk of fresh Eurozone turmoil, warns Jefferies France's mounting government debt and rising bond yields could trigger a fresh crisis at the heart of the Eurozone, with the risk of financial contagion threatening the stability of the common currency, according to a report by Jefferies GREED & fear. ANI | Updated: 30-10-2026 11:41 IST | Created: 30-10-2026 11:41 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

France's mounting government debt and rising bond yields could trigger a fresh crisis at the heart of the Eurozone, with the risk of financial contagion threatening the stability of the common currency, according to a report by Jefferies GREED & fear. The report, titled ‘From the periphery to the core’, said the scale of French government debt and its ownership had made a renewed Eurozone crisis a realistic possibility over the next year, particularly if bond yields remain elevated. “But what is scary to GREED & fear, and makes a Eurozone crisis at the core, a quite realistic prospect in the next year or so in a world where bond yields remain elevated, is the scale of French government debt and its ownership,” the report said. The concerns come amid a sharp rise in the spread between French and German government bond yields. The spread between the 10-year French government bond yield and the 10-year German bund yield widened from 55 basis points in late February to 174 basis points on October 22, its highest level since November 2011. It has since narrowed to 154 basis points, the report noted. The report highlighted France's growing debt burden, with government debt standing at around 119 per cent of GDP, or approximately 3.6 trillion euros. It also pointed to the country's high government expenditure, which has remained above 50 per cent of GDP since 1981 and is currently estimated at 57 per cent. Another key concern is the extent of foreign ownership of French government debt. According to the report, overseas investors held 58.4 per cent of French long-term general government debt securities outstanding at the end of the second quarter of 2026, the highest share since the first quarter of 2016. The report also flagged the possibility of Japanese investors selling French bonds as one factor behind the recent market pressure, while clarifying that this was an assessment rather than a confirmed explanation. Japanese institutions, including life insurers, have growing incentives to repatriate overseas investments as domestic bond yields become more attractive. Political uncertainty ahead of France's presidential elections, scheduled for April and May 2027, has added to investor concerns. The report said the election outlook was one factor behind the upward pressure on French bond yields, although it argued that the country's debt burden and ownership structure posed the more fundamental risk. It also warned that a French bond crisis would have consequences beyond the country's financial markets, given France's central position in the currency bloc. “For a French bond crisis means a crisis at the core of the Eurozone,” the report said, adding that a failure to reach an adjustment acceptable to France could lead to more dramatic outcomes, including the end of the euro and a major impact on euro-denominated assets. The report drew a comparison with the previous Eurozone debt crisis, which was largely confined to peripheral economies such as Portugal, Italy, Greece and Spain. It said the current challenge was different because the vulnerabilities were emerging in the bloc's core economies. It further cautioned that a crisis involving France could have a wider impact on European markets and investor confidence, making the country's fiscal position an increasingly important risk for the region. The report noted that the French bond market was now firmly on investors' radar, pointing to the country's high public spending, rising debt and dependence on foreign investors as key vulnerabilities. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Halloween: Tracing the centuries-old origins of ‘Trick-or-Treat’ Modern late autumn arrives wrapped in synthetic cobwebs, glowing Jack-o’-lanterns and aisles of confectionery. Halloween is widely associated with costumes, decorations, festive activities and the exchange of sweets, while its historical roots are linked to seasonal customs and religious observances. ANI | Updated: 30-10-2026 10:05 IST | Created: 30-10-2026 10:05 IST

People attend annual pre-Halloween High Heel Race in Washington, DC, US. (Photo/REUTERS). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Modern late autumn arrives wrapped in synthetic cobwebs, glowing Jack-o’-lanterns and aisles of confectionery. Halloween is widely associated with costumes, decorations, festive activities and the exchange of sweets, while its historical roots are linked to seasonal customs and religious observances. When children knock on a neighbour’s door today, they participate in a tradition that has evolved over several centuries. The practice offers an opportunity for neighbours to interact, welcome visitors and share small gifts as part of the annual Halloween celebrations. Ever wondered how these old customs evolved into the modern-day “trick-or-treat”? The origins of modern-day “trick-or-treat” can be traced to several customs practised in different parts of Europe and North America. Halloween, or All Hallows’ Eve, is observed on October 31. Over time, the occasion became associated with costumes, bonfires, lanterns and community gatherings. These customs developed alongside seasonal traditions that marked the transition from autumn to winter. One of the practices associated with Halloween was dressing up, known in some regions as “guising”. Young people visited homes, sang songs or told jokes in exchange for small gifts such as apples and coins. The tradition of wearing costumes has continued to evolve, with children and adults dressing as fictional characters, superheroes, witches and other figures during modern celebrations. Halloween also developed a tradition of playful pranks. In earlier times, young people engaged in activities such as moving garden gates, tying door handles together and soaping windows. In North America, community celebrations gradually incorporated organised activities and the distribution of treats. During the early 20th century, the practice of children visiting homes for sweets became increasingly popular, helping establish the modern tradition associated with the phrase “Trick or treat!” Another familiar Halloween custom is carving pumpkins into lanterns. Before pumpkins became widely associated with the festival, people in parts of the British Isles carved faces into turnips and other root vegetables to create lanterns. The practice travelled to North America, where pumpkins became a popular alternative because of their size and ease of carving. Today, carved pumpkins, outdoor lights and festive decorations are common features of Halloween. Homes displaying such decorations often signal their participation in the celebrations and their readiness to welcome children collecting sweets. The following day, November 1, is observed as All Saints’ Day in the Western Christian tradition. The occasion honours saints and is marked by church services, prayers and other religious observances. It forms part of Allhallowtide, a three-day period comprising All Hallows’ Eve on October 31, All Saints’ Day on November 1 and All Souls’ Day on November 2. The final day, All Souls’ Day, is dedicated to remembering the departed and praying for their souls. One historical custom associated with the occasion was “souling”, practised in parts of medieval Europe. People, including children, visited homes and received small, sweet, spiced biscuits known as soul cakes, sometimes marked with a cross. In return, they offered prayers for deceased members of the household. Over time, the practice of giving food to visitors became one of the historical customs associated with the development of door-to-door Halloween traditions. While soul cakes were part of earlier observances, modern celebrations commonly feature chocolates, sweets and other packaged treats. The exchange of small gifts remains a recognisable element of the tradition. All Souls’ Day is also associated with family remembrance. Observances in various communities have included visiting cemeteries, cleaning tombstones, lighting candles and offering prayers for deceased relatives. These practices provide families with an opportunity to remember loved ones and maintain connections with their family histories. Together, Halloween, All Saints’ Day and All Souls’ Day form a sequence of observances with distinct traditions and purposes. Halloween features costumes, decorations and community activities; All Saints’ Day honours saints; and All Souls’ Day focuses on remembering the departed. Although modern Halloween is often associated with commercial celebrations, elaborate costumes and bowls of confectionery, its customs carry echoes of older religious and folk traditions. What began as a combination of seasonal practices, community exchanges and observances dedicated to the dead has evolved over centuries into a celebration that brings neighbours together. (ANI)

item.title: DoorDash to acquire grocery delivery platform Instacart in USD 17 billion deal
item.description: US-based food delivery company DoorDash on Thursday announced an agreement to acquire grocery delivery platform Instacart in a deal valued at approximately USD 17 billion, as consolidation gathers ...
item.content:encoded:
DoorDash to acquire grocery delivery platform Instacart in USD 17 billion deal US-based food delivery company DoorDash on Thursday announced an agreement to acquire grocery delivery platform Instacart in a deal valued at approximately USD 17 billion, as consolidation gathers pace in the global food and grocery delivery market. ANI | Updated: 29-10-2026 21:38 IST | Created: 29-10-2026 21:38 IST

DoorDash logo (Photo/X@DoorDash). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US-based food delivery company DoorDash on Thursday announced an agreement to acquire grocery delivery platform Instacart in a deal valued at approximately USD 17 billion, as consolidation gathers pace in the global food and grocery delivery market. According to a joint statement issued by the two companies, DoorDash will acquire Instacart for USD 65 per share, representing a 26 per cent premium to Instacart's closing share price on October 22, the last trading day before reports of a possible transaction emerged. "DoorDash, Inc. (NASDAQ: DASH) and Maplebear Inc. (d.b.a. Instacart, NASDAQ: CART) today announced a definitive agreement under which DoorDash will acquire Instacart for a total value of $65.00 for each Instacart share, or an equity value of approximately $17 billion," the companies said in the statement. The transaction will involve at least 75 per cent cash, while DoorDash shares will account for no more than 25 per cent of the total consideration. Instacart shareholders can choose to receive cash, DoorDash shares or a combination of both, subject to certain conditions. Shares of DoorDash rose nearly 6 per cent in early US trading on Thursday, following the acquisition announcement and stronger-than-expected quarterly revenue. Instacart shares were largely unchanged at USD 58.35, according to Reuters. The acquisition comes amid growing consolidation in the global food delivery industry, as companies face rising operating costs, increasing competition and pressure to expand beyond restaurant deliveries. The industry has witnessed several major transactions, including DoorDash's acquisition of Deliveroo in 2025 and Uber's agreement to acquire Germany's Delivery Hero in July 2026. The proposed acquisition will combine DoorDash's delivery network with Instacart's grocery technology and retail partnerships, strengthening its position against large retailers such as Amazon and Walmart. Tony Xu, co-founder and CEO of DoorDash, said, "Instacart has spent years learning to do that well for grocers, while DoorDash has built a delivery network and technology that local stores rely on every day." The companies said Instacart customers could gain access to more than 50,000 additional stores. They also plan to combine DashPass and Instacart+ memberships, potentially saving subscribers an estimated USD 100 million annually. Following the acquisition, DoorDash expects to retain Instacart's brand, application and enterprise technology products. The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028, subject to Instacart shareholder approval and regulatory clearances, including antitrust review in the United States. Until then, both companies will continue operating independently. (ANI)

item.title: Israel President Herzog calls for probe into claims of foreign influence in elections, cautions against targeting Arab voters
item.description: These remarks came after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his political allies accused opponents of electoral bribery intended to drive up Arab voting numbers.
item.content:encoded:
Israel President Herzog calls for probe into claims of foreign influence in elections, cautions against targeting Arab voters These remarks came after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his political allies accused opponents of electoral bribery intended to drive up Arab voting numbers. ANI | Updated: 29-10-2026 17:53 IST | Created: 29-10-2026 17:53 IST

Israeli President Isaac Herzog (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Israeli President Isaac Herzog has stated that he held discussions with Central Elections Committee chief Noam Sohlberg and Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) chief David Zini following Sohlberg’s request to probe allegations of external interference in Tuesday's election. According to the Times of Israel, Herzog, speaking from the President’s Residence, emphasised the necessity of a rigorous review while warning against unfairly maligning the broader Arab populace. “I am closely following developments in the investigation into the suspicions reported this morning. The integrity of elections is a paramount value in a democracy. The evidence and suspicions must be thoroughly investigated, and the offenders must be investigated and punished to the fullest extent of the law,” he stated. These remarks came after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his political allies accused opponents of electoral bribery intended to drive up Arab voting numbers. Herzog cautioned, "But even at a moment like this, we must avoid tarnishing an entire community that sought to exercise its right to vote and take an active part in democracy.” The Times of Israel further noted that Herzog renewed his plea to political leaders to enter upcoming government negotiations with an “open” mind and prioritise solely “what is in the best interests of the country”. Subsequently, the Times of Israel, citing Hebrew media outlets, reported that Shin Bet chief David Zini met yesterday with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to deliberate on the foreign election interference probe. According to those reports, the meeting was requested by the Shin Bet, which had already initiated its investigation into the matter prior to election day. Additionally, Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot met with Zini this morning, the Times of Israel reported, as per the party statement. “During the meeting, he was updated on the suspicions regarding foreign interference in the election in Israel. Eisenkot offered his support for the Shin Bet and law enforcement officials for a swift and transparent investigation,” the party stated. This comes as the Shin Bet probes allegations of possible foreign interference in the recently concluded Knesset elections after the decision of the Israel Election Committee to order an investigation into allegations, which has created a political firestorm in Jerusalem. The call to action follows Israeli Central Elections Committee Chair Justice Noam Sohlberg asking Shin Bet chief David Zini to investigate allegations of foreign interference in Tuesday’s election. Shin Bet is currently probing allegations of Qatari influence in the recently concluded elections. (ANI)
